body:
Per the read-only audit `backend-paywall-audit.md` (commit `a9c1956f`), the following student-reachable controllers do NOT carry `ClientEntitlementGuard` but per `ENGINEERING_RULES.md §4` and the product brief, they are paid surfaces. Mobile PR https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/186 lands a defence-in-depth client paywall covering these surfaces today, but the server should be canonical (R20).

## P0 — must add `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, ClientEntitlementGuard)`

- [ ] **`HolisticInsightsController`** — `GET /insights/holistic` (`src/insights/holistic-insights.controller.ts:17-24`). AI insights generation is explicitly flagged as a paid surface in the product brief.
- [ ] **`SchedulingController`** — currently no class-level guard at all (relies on global `JwtAuthGuard`). At minimum, gate write paths: `POST /scheduling/sessions`, `POST /scheduling/sessions/:id/reschedule`, `POST /scheduling/sessions/:id/cancel`. (`src/scheduling/scheduling.controller.ts:51-53`)
- [ ] **`ClientMessagingController`** — `POST /messages` (send) and `POST /messages/voice-upload` (voice notes). Voice notes / coach commentary are flagged as paid in the brief and the Phase 6C env vars (`VOICE_NOTE_MAX_DURATION_SEC`, etc.) confirm first-class status. Leave `GET /messages` and `GET /messages/unread-count` open so polling envelopes don't break. (`src/messaging/client-messaging.controller.ts:27-28`)

## P1 — product decision needed (paid or intentionally free?)

`/bloodwork/*`, `/weight/*`, `/water/*`, `/habits/*`, `/lessons/*`, `/timeline/*`, `/build-week/*`, `/nudges/*`, `/recipes/*`, `/lists/*`, `/prep-guide`, `/me/first-win/*`, `/me/leaderboard/*` — each is student-reachable with only `JwtAuthGuard`. Whether to gate is a product question. Document the decision in `docs/tier-classification.md` extended with a "Client surface" section.

## P1 — regression guard

- [ ] Add a Jest spec (shape like `test/module-graph.spec.ts`) that walks the Nest container, finds every controller a `student`-role user can reach, and asserts each is either in an explicit `studentFreeList` or has `ClientEntitlementGuard` mounted. Without this, the next paid feature will silently regress.

## P2 — default-deny direction

The current decorator is `@SkipClientEntitlement()` — an opt-out. Consider registering `ClientEntitlementGuard` as an `APP_GUARD` plus an explicit `@PublicForClients()` opt-in allowlist so the default-deny direction matches the rule's intent. This is the most durable fix; the per-controller TODOs above are interim.

## Why now

Mobile is shipping a client-side paywall (PR #186) as defence in depth, but the server is the canonical authority for entitlement (Rule 20). Until the P0 items land, the client paywall is the ONLY thing protecting these surfaces from unentitled users on a healthy network path.
title: Server-side entitlement gaps surfaced by mobile paywall wire-up
